description: The Global Library of School Infrastructure is a repository developed under the World Bank's Global Program for Safer Schools of data and information on the structural performance and vulnerability of school buildings and on options to reduce their seismic risk. According to the UCL EPICentre project page, its technical basis was developed by Dina D'Ayala and Rohit Kumar Adhikari at UCL with a team at Universidad de los Andes in Bogotá, with case studies in Nepal, El Salvador, Peru, the Dominican Republic, Colombia and other countries between 2016 and 2020. The work set up a uniform data collection system for school infrastructure, a global structural taxonomy of school buildings, field verification of databases and fragility functions for school typologies, all documented in the publicly accessible online library; because school buildings share typologies across countries, the tools, vulnerability functions and retrofit solutions can be reused. Coverage: mainly public school infrastructure in developing countries. Access: the GPSS website, which returned 403 to automated reading on the day. Licence: not read; free to access. Caveats: the provider's own pages could not be read, so facts come from the UCL partner site. Simulation uses are fragility and vulnerability functions for school building types in earthquake risk and retrofit prioritisation. Related records: the GEM Building Taxonomy and the Central Sulawesi school buildings inventory.
